sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Fuliiru language' (the page 'Joba language' redirects here; infobox: job / joba1238 = Joba (Vira), Guthrie JD.63,631), accessed 2026-09-17
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology section covers Fuliiru only (two-way H/L tone contrast, after Van Otterloo 2011); no statement on stress and no Joba-specific data.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalogue, 'OLAC resources in and about the Joba language' (as of 19 Nov 2021, Internet Archive copy)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; the only 'language description' listed is the Glottolog record; other resource is the Ethnologue entry. No archive holds Joba materials.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed. Entry 'Joba' [job] (the Internet Archive copy)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Alternate names Kijoba, Kivira, Loba, Vira; 10,000 (1989 SIL); Sud-Kivu, Uvira territory, north and northwest of Uvira; classification Narrow Bantu, J, Ruanda-Rundi (D.631); 'Also use Fuliiru [flr]'.

sources.citation: Maho, Jouni F. 2009. NUGL Online: The online version of the New Updated Guthrie List, a referential classification of the Bantu languages. p. 59
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; classification only: 'JD63.... Fuliiro flr / JD631.... Vira job, Joba' (Vira/Joba as a sub-entry of Fuliiro in the JD60 Ruanda-Rundi group).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 reference table for joba1238 (Hammarström et al.), queried 2026-09-17: Schoenbrun 1994, 1997; Verhulpen 1936; Bastin, Coupez & Mann 1999; Meeussen 1953; Cleire 1942; Weis 1959; Ize-Sense et al. 1984; Meeussen 1951 'Notes vira, non publié'

sources.note: Nothing; 0 descriptive references (no grammar, sketch, phonology or dictionary) for Joba. The only description-type item is Meeussen's unpublished 1951 'Notes vira' (Tervuren; keywords grm, phn; 'Referred to by Paluku (1998:356)').

sources.citation: Any SIL Eastern Congo Group sociolinguistic survey or Congolese university mémoire on Kivira/Kiviila (ISP Bukavu, UNIKIN, Université de Lubumbashi) — none identified by title.

sources.citation: Van Otterloo, Karen. 2011. The Kifuliiru Language, Vol. 1: Phonology, Tone and Morphological Derivation. Dallas: SIL International (Publications in Linguistics 146). ISBN 978-1-55671-261-6 (2-vol. set OCLC 747807710).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Full phonology/tone description of the closest relative (Maho JD63; Joba = JD631). Likely contains an explicit statement on stress/penultimate lengthening and possibly remarks on the Vira variety; the best proxy if no Joba-specific source can be had.

sources.citation: Jouannet, Francis. 1984. Phonologie du kifuliru (langue bantoue du groupe J). Paris: SELAF (Société d'études linguistiques et anthropologiques de France 94), 74 pp. ISBN 9782877230162.

sources.note: Earlier phonology of the sister language Fuliiru (consonants, vowels, tone, downdrift per the 1984 IDERIC bibliographic note); may state whether Fuliiru/Vira has accent beyond tone.

sources.citation: Meeussen, Achille Emiel. 1951. Notes vira, non publié. Tervuren: Musée Royal du Congo Belge (MRCB) [now RMCA archives].

sources.note: The only item on record with grammar/phonology content for Vira/Joba itself (Glottolog keywords grm, phn; cited by Paluku 1998: 356). Meeussen's field notes normally record tone; would settle whether anything at all is said about accent.
